title: Strict logarithmic infinitesimal lifting predicates
statement:
Use log structures, geometric monoid stalks, their structural maps and the unit-pushout chart predicate of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], arbitrary-scheme log morphisms and their equality with a composite and strict etale restrictions from [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation], and the arbitrary-scheme fine predicate of [def-trf-fine-log-etale-descent-datum]. For a log morphism $f:(X,M)\to(Y,N)$ of arbitrary schemes, equality $fa=bi$ means equality of the scheme maps and of the log sheaf maps. It can be expressed by the existence of a common composite equal to both. A log morphism $g:(V,L)\to(T,K)$ is strict when the canonical map from the log structure associated to $g^{-1}K$ is an isomorphism. Here inverse image is the etale inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and association is the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the unit pushout. Equivalently, at every geometric point $t$ of $V$ let $\varphi:K_{g(t)}\to L_t$ be the map prescribed on every relative pointed etale section diagram by $g$. The product map $K_{g(t)}\times\mathcal O_{V,t}^{\times}\to L_t$, $(m,u)\mapsto\varphi(m)u$, is surjective and its kernel congruence is generated by $(me,u)\sim(m,\beta(e)u)$ for $\beta(e)$ a unit, with $\beta=\alpha_{L,t}\varphi$. Thus its actual unit-pushout quotient is isomorphic to $L_t$ by the canonical map.

A fine test square for $f$ consists of arbitrary fine log schemes $(T_0,L_0)$ and $(T,L)$, log morphisms $i:(T_0,L_0)\to(T,L)$, $a:(T_0,L_0)\to(X,M)$, $b:(T,L)\to(Y,N)$ with $fa=bi$, with $i$ strict and its underlying map a first-order thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. Define the etale-local lifting predicate by requiring a log lift on etale neighbourhoods covering $T$, where etaleness is [def-weil-etale-morphism] and every neighbourhood has the pulled-back log structure. More explicitly, for each point $t\in T$ there is an etale $v:V\to T$ whose image contains $t$, with its strict pulled-back log structure, and a log map $c:V\to X$ such that $fc=bv$. On $R=T_0\times_TV$, the scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], take the strict etale pullback $v_0:R\to T_0$ of $L_0$. The log map $j:R\to V$ has underlying map the second projection and is determined by $vj=iv_0$; require $cj=av_0$. Pointwise existence is equivalently a jointly surjective family of such neighbourhoods. Define the unique-global-lifting predicate by requiring for every fine test square exactly one log morphism $c:(T,L)\to(X,M)$ with $fc=b$ and $ci=a$. No Noetherian or saturation hypothesis is imposed on any test scheme.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1 and X Proposition 1.2, pp.136--139; the referenced primary source Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie, 1.3--1.4 and 3.1--3.3, pp.192--193 and 200--201, read at https://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/p-adic_periods/Kato_log-structures.pdf.
